recipes.name: Glazed Meatloaf
ingredients_raw: 3 slices bread, broken up into small pieces

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine ketchup, brown sugar, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, and mustard powder in a small bowl.
Combine ground beef, bread, onion, egg, bouillon, and remaining lemon juice in a separate large bowl. Add in 1/3 of the ketchup mixture from the small bowl. Mix well and place in a 5x9-inch loaf pan.
Bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour. Drain any excess fat, coat with remaining ketchup mixture, and bake for 10 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Glazed Meatloaf
raw_recipe.description: This glazed meatloaf recipe features ground beef, egg, bread, and onions. It gets topped with sweet and sour glaze and baked to comforting perfection.

review.reviewBody:
My children didn't even know what meatloaf was, as I had never made it before. My childhood memories of meatloaf did not provide any encouragement for me to make that dish for my family. 

When I ran across this recipe, it was so highly rated that I decided to try it out. My family loved it! I have made it many times since. I even made it for a friend's family when she was convalescing after surgery. Her son said, "This is better than your meatloaf, Mom!" :) She requested the recipe and now makes it for her family. 

I used to use the slices of bread but I really like using dry bread crumbs better (about 1 cup). I don't end up with any visible chunks of bread in the loaf.

Very moist and tasty! A few substitutes: I used 1 small can tomato sauce in the meat mixture in place of lemon juice and ketchup mixture; eliminated beef bouillon granules and added salt, pepper and garlic powder; and used 2 slices of bread instead of 3. I've also made this dish just using ketchup as glaze and it comes out great! I baked potatoes at the same time; total cooking time was closer to 1 1/2 hrs. My husband and grown children love this meat loaf! Grandkids don't like the onions; onions should be chopped fine or they don't cook through. This dish also cooks best with very lean beef, under 7% to 15% fat. Serve with corn and a simple tossed salad for a great, easy meal.
Separated into smaller tins for later use. Added strips pre cooked bacon to bottom of pan for added flavor.

My family and I like this recipe very much. I have made a few adjustments but nothing major. I use half cup of panko bread crumbs instead of slices of bread. I also add about 2 cloves of minced garlic. I use 1.5 tsp of "Better Than Bouillon" beef base instead of granules. Line the bottom of a loaf pan with 2 slices of bread to soak up excess grease.
I revised this recipe. Added dried beef onion soup, worcestershire sauce, and made with tomato based brown gravy instead

This was excellent, I however was trying a lighter version, so I used ground turkey instead of beef, I also used light brown sugar. I did not have the lemon so as someone else suggested I replaced the lemon with white vinegar. I also used italian bread crumbs about 1/2-3/4 cup. I managed to bring the calories per serving down to 360 with the ground turkey, next time, because there will be a next time, I will use ground turkey breast and that will bring the calories down to 300 per serving. This recipe is a keeper. oh on a side note I did not have the bouillon granules so I took 2 cubes and used my cheese grater to grind them up, I think it was more than the amount called for but it was wonderful !

Best meatloaf I have made in years! Everyone loved the flavor! My husband and my seven year old especially liked it. I loved it! Will make regularly. (Substituted some onion powder for chopped; subbed some worcestershire for beef broth; added some garlic powder. Flavor was like a unique bbq sauce almost. The sauce would be great on grilled ribs!

I added salt and pepper, parmesan, bread crumbs instead of bread and sautéed 2 garlic cloves plus the onion before mixing it in. 

I also took previous advice and used a couple spoonfuls of brown sugar instead and it worked out really well.

Great idea for weeknights!!!

I picked this recipe because it does not use milk. We don't drink milk. so we never have any in the house to cook with.

This is an easy recipe that turns out great......I used some old beef bouillon. Next time will use fresh....Anyway...this turned out great as is. For the bread crumbs, I toasted two end crusts and one piece, then used some kitchen shears to cut into small chunks.

This recipe is easy to customize...enjoy, I did...and yes. I will make it again.
I use Better Than Bouillon in place if the Bouillon granules

This recipe is a great base to start off with. I hide a bunch of veggies in this meatloaf and my kids are none the wiser. Finely chopped (in the processor) fresh tomatoes, red and green bell peppers, onions, lots of garlic, and even kale! I didn't have any lemon for the glaze so I used apple cider vinegar instead. Great taste. I did not mix any of the ketchup concoction into the meatloaf, but did add some Worcestershire and smoked paprika. Used breadcrumbs instead of bread pieces, and doubled the eggs. Now that I know my kids are a fan and they're eating lots of vegetables, I'll be making this meatloaf again and again!

Amazing meatloaf and husband said it’s a keeper and it is better than my Momma’s meatloaf. I had no mustard in the house, nor did my neighbors have any. It is worth the effort and our grandsons loved it!!
I was nervous about the lemon juice... but wow this was amazing!! Definitely making again! Make ahead and freeze. Reheats great.
Best meatloaf I have ever had. My family loves it!

This is one of the first recipes I ever tried on All Recipes. My son and mother usually don't like meatloaf, but they love this recipe! I do increase the glaze by about 1/2 because we like it saucy! Definitely a keeper. Note: I have since been diagnosed with Celiac Disease and now make it with Gluten-Free bread crumbs in place of the bread (about 1/2 cup) soaked in 1/2 cup beef broth and I don't use the bouillon cube and it is just as delicious!
We enjoyed. Substituted Ground Turkey for the beef! Delicious!
Absolutely love the glaze on this meatloaf. I would double it. I do make my meatloaf differently though but use this glaze.
Love this recipe. Been using it for years.

I used this very recipe when I first discovered allrecipes.com about 10 years ago. For a person raised on the dry, cracked, and tasteless meatloaf, (sorry, Mom!) this was a leap of faith for me. And I’m glad I jumped! My family has always approved of it, and we will continue to do so for many years.
